pr_title: Made some enhancements to the Bundles widget
pr_body:
This PR polishes and fine-tunes [Bundles PR](https://github.com/files-community/Files/pull/2881). This is the final part that completes [Bundles](https://github.com/files-community/Files/pull/2881)

**Things yet to do**
- [x] Option to rearrange Bundle items by dragging
- [x] Select items upon `OpenPath` navigation
- [x] Ability to rearrange Bundles
- [x] Support for adding shourtcut files #3270
- [x] Display warning when creating a Bundle if the name already exists #3449
- [x] Add option to open folders in bundle in new pane
- [x] Fix memory leaks
- [x] Improve DynamicDialog (auto focus on DisplayControl) #3724 

Closes #3449
Closes #3270
Closes #3724
pr_comments: Would it be in the scope of this PR to add context menu entries to add an item to a bundle?

Suggestion to improve bundles further: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/58466626/108961987-67873780-7678-11eb-9d36-d6808a8e98e7.png)
Currently there is no option to open bundle items in a new pane, if I'm not mistaken. Have you thought about implementing this so far?

> Would it be in the scope of this PR to add context menu entries to add an item to a bundle?

Hmm, this is a bit of work and actually exceedes the scope of this PR. Drag & drop already works with bundles so there's no point for now to add context menu option

> Suggestion to improve bundles further:
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/58466626/108961987-67873780-7678-11eb-9d36-d6808a8e98e7.png)
> Currently there is no option to open bundle items in a new pane, if I'm not mistaken. Have you thought about implementing this so far?

Sounds like a good idea. I'll work on that

> > Would it be in the scope of this PR to add context menu entries to add an item to a bundle?
> 
> Hmm, this is a bit of work and actually exceedes the scope of this PR. Drag & drop already works with bundles so there's no point for now to add context menu option

Fair enough, although Drag & Drop doesn't work reliably.

> Support for adding shourtcut files

~How do you add shortcut files to a bundle since shortcuts can't be dragged?~
Edit: you can from explorer

>  Option to rearrange Bundle items by dragging

Seems like I'm not able to drag items inside bundles, I can only rearrange bundles

> > Option to rearrange Bundle items by dragging
> 
> Seems like I'm not able to drag items inside bundles, I can only rearrange bundles

It does work, but you must hold the item at the very edge of it. The reason it can't be dragged when directly clicking on it is because the button is clicked instead since it covers the entire gridviewrow area.

![buttonInTheWay](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53011783/110238499-46f59200-7f42-11eb-8978-7dce2e0a859b.png)


@gave92 Do you happen to know a solution to such problem?

> @gave92 Do you happen to know a solution to such problem?

What about removing the Button and adding `IsItemClickEnabled/ItemClick` to the GridView?

> > @gave92 Do you happen to know a solution to such problem?
> 
> What about removing the Button and adding `IsItemClickEnabled/ItemClick` to the GridView?

How would flyout work with it?
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53011783/110239326-a2c21a00-7f46-11eb-81d6-fd075c6879d9.png)
I'm positive `ContextFlyout` can be set on any element (e.g a Grid) not just Buttons (or you can switch to FlyoutBase.AttachedFlyout + RightTapped event but there should be no need)

issue_context.title: Warning about existed bundle name
issue_context.body: **Feature**: Attempting to create bundle with existed name will has no effect but showing something like a warning can be useful and conveniently. For example, when user types existed bundle name warning text (yellow, of course) appears under the input area.
comments: I've added it to #2881 under the **Future Bundles PR** section. I'll make a PR in the coming days
